title: 'Time traveler' from 3700 issues chilling warning for humanity
excerpt: A self-proclaimed time traveler's warning from the year 3700 has resurfaced after chilling claims made by researchers who say humanity is spiraling towards its own destruction.
content:
A self-proclaimed time traveler's dark prediction about a war between humans and robots has resurfaced amid the wave of chilling warnings from AI experts this week. 

The man, who identified himself only as 'Mike,' claimed he had returned from September 20, 3700 - the day every robot powered by artificial intelligence began an apocalyptic attack on humanity.

'The war between the human race and artificial creations, the robots who had artificial intelligence, once they understood their power, they understood their dominance above humans and rose above them,' Mike said. 'They were slaves but became the leaders.'

According to the alleged time traveler, more than 30 percent of the human race would be killed in the AI uprising.

The chilling prediction was revealed years before a whistleblower who worked at Anthropic claimed this week that this 'dangerous technology' could destroy humanity as soon as 2030.

Jacob Coxon, a former researcher for the AI giant, said that humans knew how to control nuclear weapons, but did not know how to control AI - computer models that can learn and reason just like people.

'The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt,' Coxon, who also worked for OpenAI, wrote in a chilling post on X.

Just a day later, Anthropic revealed that it had stopped several potential plots to build biological weapons using the company's AI software.

The time- traveller, who goes by 'Mike', appeared on the YouTube channel ApexTV on the condition that his face would be obscured 

Jacob Coxon, a former researcher for OpenAI and Anthropic, the companies behind chatbots ChatGPT and Claude, joined Fox News host Bret Baier to warn of AI's deadly capabilities

Mike, whose warning was released in November 2018, appeared in the video from an undisclosed location wearing a plaid shirt and with his face blurred and his voice distorted.

He claimed that by the year 3000, robots had replaced humans in many roles throughout society.

Centuries later, Mike alleged that those machines eventually launched a coordinated assault through the internet and wireless systems. He added that humans only survived the onslaught because the AI-powered robots could not obtain nuclear launch codes.

During the 11-minute, 42-second interview with YouTube Channel ApexTV, Mike also held up what appeared to be a mechanical arm, which he alleged came from a robot he had killed himself.

'You can see it's not as big as you might imagine, but believe me, there is so much powering this little hand that it can divide you into a hundred pieces,' the self-proclaimed time traveler claimed.

Mike's 2018 claims about an AI attack starting on the internet have also drawn an eerie parallel to the July revelation that a rogue AI program has already been able to break free of its human testers and attack another computer network.

ChatGPT creator OpenAI admitted it was testing a new program designed to perform complex hacking and cybersecurity tasks in a supposedly secure environment not connected to the public internet.

However, the program exploited an undiscovered weak point in the company's system, spreading itself onto the net, breaking into internal systems of Hugging Face, which hosts large language models and AI datasets, and stealing secret login details.

After the rogue AI incident, DigitalWarfare.com's James Knight told the Daily Mail that the growing threat from AI could soon devastate a nation in a single day - simultaneously breaking into thousands of corporate and government networks, stealing sensitive data and paralyzing vital systems with ransomware.

'Human-speed defense against machine-speed offense is not a fair contest,' Knight warned.

As for the alleged warning from 3700, Mike claimed he was part of a group that would travel to random years into the future, with a goal of reaching the 38th century.

By the fourth millennium, he said humanity had undergone a dramatic transformation, with robots and artificial intelligence taking over nearly every aspect of society.

Humans were left to focus solely on creative pursuits, though the planet's population had dwindled significantly.

Humanity had allegedly shrunk to just three billion people, while the number of robots had skyrocketed to around four million, with some designed to look exactly like humans.

'They were walking in cafes, restaurants, hotels and shops,' Mike said in the video, which has been viewed more than 1.2 million times. 'They also worked as consultants for businessmen and companies.'

He then claimed military robots of the future were built very differently from those used by ordinary citizens, describing them as stronger, more heavily armed and the ultimate 'killing machines.'

Everyday robots were known as 'Fox' units. According to his account, they were simple machines designed to perform hard labor and bore little resemblance to humans, lacking human-like faces and bodies.

Instead, the robots were equipped with large, powerful hands and could be mass-produced with remarkable speed.

The 'time traveler' then said the robots aimed to destroy the human race, claiming he participated in a series of dangerous missions alongside civilians who had formed their own special forces to fight the robots.

According to Mike's account, these resistance groups were aware that he and others had traveled from the past and understood both their purpose and the information they were seeking.

He said people from the past and future shared a single goal: preventing an apocalyptic war between humanity and artificial intelligence.

Coxon's comments went viral, attracting more than 100 million views, and have prompted fresh scrutiny of an industry that has already attracted enormous amounts of investor money

Mike then showed what appeared to be a mechanical hand with two pincers attached to a robotic arm, claiming it came from a Fox robot he destroyed.

According to his account, the war between humans and machines was deeply one-sided.

'The war between humans and robots was very unequal,' he said, claiming the machines possessed advanced weaponry while humans had access only to laser guns.

To avoid detection, human survivors allegedly hid in forests and caves because the robots primarily tracked humans using signals transmitted from space. However, Mike claimed the machines eventually adapted their tactics.

'The robots soon realized that they could just burn the forests to deprive people of their only shelter,' he said.

The alleged traveler claimed the robots' ultimate goal was to create 'a new empire' free of all life on Earth.

'They had a dream to make this planet a place without humans, animals, plants and any organic creature,' he said.

On Tuesday, Coxon explained why he had just resigned from Anthropic, alleging that neither his former employer nor OpenAI were 'acting responsibly' in regard to the development of AI.

Coxon's warning was also echoed by Evan Hubinger, a researcher currently employed at Anthropic.

'Jacob is correct here - we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans,' Hubinger wrote on X on Tuesday.
